basis.governing_question: How can Metalúrgica Norte cut conversion cost at its Braga plant and put the improvements in place?

phases.name: Diagnostic
phases.objective_one_line: Establish conversion cost per part at the Braga plant and size the improvements that could lower it.

gate.label: Initiatives go/no-go
gate.decision: Which sized initiatives go into implementation at the plant, and which stop here?

phases.name: Implementation
phases.objective_one_line: Put the agreed improvements in place at the plant and show their effect on conversion cost per part.

gate.label: Final readout
gate.decision: Approve the results against the baseline and the handover to the plant team?

workstreams.name: Conversion cost baseline
workstreams.answers: What is conversion cost per part at the Braga plant today, built up from cost data?
activities: Collect conversion cost data for the Braga plant
Build conversion cost per part from the cost data
Test the baseline with the people who run the plant

workstreams.name: Line loss analysis
workstreams.answers: On which production lines, and in which losses, does conversion cost build up at the Braga plant?
activities: Observe the production lines on the floor, two at a time
Quantify losses on each line from operational data
Interview the people who run each line about losses

workstreams.name: Improvement sizing
workstreams.answers: Which improvements can lower conversion cost per part by a measurable amount, and how much is each worth?
activities: List candidate improvements from the loss analysis
Size each one's effect on cost per part with cost data
Set out the sized list for the go/no-go decision

workstreams.name: Line improvement rollout
workstreams.answers: How are the chosen improvements put in place on the plant's lines, and in what order?
activities: Prepare each improvement with the people on the line
Show readiness at the first workshop before any go-live
Bring improvements to go-live, two at a time

workstreams.name: Cost per part tracking
workstreams.answers: Does conversion cost per part fall against the baseline as the improvements go live?
activities: Set up the cost-per-part tracker against the baseline
Read cost data on each line after every go-live
Report results against the baseline at each review

workstreams.name: Plant team capability
workstreams.answers: What must the plant team know and do to own the improvements after handover?
activities: Define what the plant team will own after handover
Train and coach plant staff on the running improvements
Hand the tracker and routines to the plant team

workstreams.name: Improvements in operation
workstreams.answers: Do the improvements keep running on the lines once live, without slipping back?
activities: Observe the improved lines in running operation
Check with line staff that the changes are still followed
Log slippage in operational data and agree fixes

deliverables.name: Conversion cost per part baseline for the Braga plant
Line loss findings from the first lines observed
Line loss analysis by production line and loss type
Sized improvement pack for the go/no-go decision
Go-live readiness pack for each improvement
Cost per part results after the first go-lives
Final readout pack: results against baseline and handover
Plant team training record and tracker handover

events.label: Kick-off
events.purpose: Start the work and agree plant data access
events.decision: Which Braga plant data and which plant staff can the team access from week 1?
agenda: Present the two phases, workstreams and gate decisions
Review the data and people the baseline and line loss work need
Decide the plant data and staff access for the first weeks

events.label: Check-in: first findings
events.purpose: Review baseline and first loss findings
events.decision: Which loss types from the first findings go forward into improvement sizing?
agenda: Present the conversion cost per part baseline for Braga
Review the line loss findings from the first lines observed
Decide which loss types go into improvement sizing

events.label: Initiatives go/no-go
events.purpose: Decide which sized initiatives go ahead
events.decision: Which sized initiatives go into implementation at the plant, and which stop here?
agenda: Present the line loss analysis by production line and loss type
Review the sized improvement pack for the go/no-go decision
Decide which sized initiatives go into implementation

events.label: Workshop 1: readiness
events.purpose: Review readiness before anything goes live
events.decision: Which improvements are cleared to go live, and which need more readiness work?
agenda: Present the go-live readiness pack for each improvement
Review the cost-per-part tracker set against the baseline
Decide which improvements are cleared to go live

events.label: Workshop 2: early results
events.purpose: Review early results and plant ownership
events.decision: Which improvements need corrective action before the final readout?
agenda: Present the cost per part results after the first go-lives
Review the go-live records and the plant team ownership definition
Decide which improvements need corrective action

events.label: Final readout
events.decision: Approve the results against the baseline and the handover to the plant team?
agenda: Present the final readout pack: results against baseline and handover
Review the operation check, slippage log and plant team training record
Decide whether to approve the results and the plant team handover

architect_notes: Engagement length is not given; the 15 to 19 weeks are an estimate to confirm before this plan becomes a quote.
Implementation assumes at least 5 weeks of cost data after the last go-live, so any change in cost per part can be measured.
Implementation takes the middle of its 9 to 13 week estimate; slower go-lives or a late cost-data close would push it to 13.
Four improvements carried into Implementation is assumed; every two more or fewer move that phase by 2 to 3 weeks. Confirm after the Diagnostic.
Three production lines come from public research and need the client's confirmation; they set the Diagnostic length.
No Measurement phase: tracking against the baseline stays inside Implementation; confirm whether the client wants tracking after the engagement ends.

sub_questions.question: What is conversion cost per part at the Braga plant today, and where does it build up?
Which improvements can lower conversion cost per part by a measurable amount, and how much is each worth?
How are the chosen improvements put in place at the plant, and in what order?
Do the improvements keep running at the plant, and does cost per part fall against the baseline?

phases.name: Diagnostic

work.unit: Plant conversion cost baseline per part from cost data
Production line observed on the floor with loss analysis

phases.why: Baseline first, then three lines observed two at a time; the second round puts the top one week above the archetype's 3 to 6.

phases.name: Implementation

work.unit: Improvement put in place on the lines and brought to go-live
Running period after last go-live for cost data to show the effect

phases.why: Four improvements put in place two at a time on the three lines, then a running period so cost data can show the effect.

sizing.levers: Carry only the largest sized improvements into Implementation and run more at once; the running period after the last go-live is the floor.
